author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Playstation 2 Dev - Better Texturing (C and Lua Programming on PS2SDK)
summary: A PS2SDK live-coding session builds DMA REF texture uploads and revises the texture abstraction so assets can move from main memory into scarce VRAM during a frame instead of requiring one static preload phase.

blocks.text: The stream begins from a concrete rendering failure, reviews the previous attempt, returns to triangle output, and then spends its main implementation block on DMA REF texture transfer. The stated goal is mid-frame uploading: PS2 VRAM is limited, but bandwidth between RAM and graphics memory can support a design that cycles texture data as rendering progresses. Watching the abstraction change alongside the low-level transfer path shows why an engine interface must express lifetime and movement, not merely return a permanent texture handle.

This is one development revision inside a larger homebrew engine, not a general guarantee that mid-frame uploads are free or optimal. Public metadata omits texture formats, transfer sizes, synchronization points and before-and-after timing, while a live stream can include provisional fixes later replaced in the repository. Its strongest evidence is the public code and named DMA strategy. Viewers should inspect the linked commit history before reusing the abstraction and budget transfer time alongside draw submission.
